author: The Dundalk Eagle
title: See Dundalk on the big screen like never before - NewsBreak
text:
7 hours ago
Who doesn't love a good evening at the movies?
Last week, I had the exciting opportunity to catch the local premiere of "The Baltimorons" at the Senator Theater — and to my elation, I saw snippets of our own Dundalk, including the Key Bridge, on screen. (An exclusive Dundalk Eagle boots-on-the-ground report: I sat two rows ahead of the film's writer and star, Michael Strassner. He spilled his popcorn everywhere.)
In this week's newsletter, I included my review on "The Baltimorons."
You might not be able to tell from the Dundalk Eagle's regular hard news coverage, but film criticism was my first true love in writing. From humble beginnings at my high school's tiny online newspaper to an entire undergraduate thesis on the future of film criticism as a craft, I have dedicated hours of my life to watching and writing about movies.
Although I don't get to flex that muscle as often anymore, I had a blast writing my review. I hope you enjoy reading it as much as I enjoyed assembling the article and attending the premiere.
Also, I want to remind all of our readers about an exciting development on the Dundalk Eagle's website.
Do you love puzzles? The Dundalk Eagle is considering adding a daily puzzles page to dundalkeagle.com. We are looking for readers to test it and give us their opinion on the puzzles. Interested? Contact Executive Editor Jim Johnson at jjohnson@chespub.com .
Also in this newsletter: A fire at the waste water treatment plant, Fort Holabird's fate, Dundalk's Charlie Kirk vigil, and new plans for the former Heritage Food Market.
Thank you for reading, and if you enjoy our newsletter, please do not forget to subscribe.
